doc.summary: ========== Fixed slirp configuration (QEMU -nic user) ==========
Linux poll(2) event bits (struct pollfd), shared by net_sys_poll and kfd_poll_revents.
QEMU masks the RCR ring-size bits (11-12) out of writes, so its legacy receive ring is always 8 KB.
doc.description: The guest ring must match: with a larger ring the guest read pointer and QEMU's 8 KB write wrap disagree and the tail of every frame that crosses 8192 is lost.

doc.summary: The RTL8139 ring is 8K + 16 bytes (datasheet, RBLEN 00): the chip may write up to 16 bytes past the 8 KB the reader indexes, so the buffer carries that tail, or the NIC writes into the next heap chunk.
RCR: accept broadcast/multicast/phys (the ring size bits are ignored by QEMU anyway).
